476b5c84bf.q: How do you identify when you've become the backup plan in your business operations?
476b5c84bf.a: You become the backup plan when something needs to get done and technically it's not yours to do anymore, but you're still thinking about it with a mental note to check on it before the end of the day. Even if everything is fine, you step in because you already know that if it doesn't happen the way it's supposed to, you'll catch it. This means you're carrying more responsibility mentally than what shows up on your actual to-do list.
476b5c84bf.e: 319: Stop Building a Business You Have to Keep Rescuing
476b5c84bf.rq: Being able to figure things out is a great skill set to have as an entrepreneur. I just don't want your business to always need you to figure out the same things.

7c88ba29cc.q: What is the difference between solving problems and handling problems in business?
7c88ba29cc.a: Solving problems means addressing the root cause so it doesn't happen again, while handling problems is just taking care of what's in front of you and moving on. When you handle a problem, the same version of it often comes back a month later because you may not have dealt with what caused it in the first place. Being really good at problem solving can work against you because you know how to handle it, so you do, but the business never really has to change.

323a369146.q: Why is constantly rescuing your business financially unsustainable?
323a369146.a: When you keep financially rescuing your business month after month, you're absorbing the cost of the problem in time and mental energy. If you bring in more money but keep ending up in the same tight position, more money by itself won't fix it. You may have a good month but still feel the same pressure sooner than expected. What matters is understanding what the money keeps having to rescue rather than assuming more revenue will solve it.

aefa890ce2.q: What should you ask instead of how to get better at rescuing your business?
aefa890ce2.a: Instead of asking how to get better at rescue, ask what your business keeps asking you to build. When you constantly have to remember something, maybe that thing needs somewhere to live other than your head. Look at places where you keep having to step in and ask what would make that rescue less necessary. The solution might be smaller than you think and doesn't always require new software or complicated systems.

5370f9ad75.q: How much time spent repeatedly solving the same problem makes the five-minute solution expensive?
5370f9ad75.a: If doing something yourself takes five minutes in the moment but you're doing it every week for the next three years, that five-minute solution becomes really expensive over time. At some point you have to give yourself the time to build what the business keeps asking you for, because repeating a quick fix multiple times across months and years accumulates significant cost in your attention and time.
